body.x: UNIUNI Corp. (CEO Han Sooyeon) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10. The company specializes in creating safe, privacy-conscious environments that use advanced technology to enhance dignity and independence for all, especially individuals with disabilities.

UNIUNI’s SAVVY Accessible Restroom, which received a CES Innovation Award for Accessibility & AgeTech, is designed to ensure the safety and privacy of restrooms for individuals with disabilities. The system uses deep learning to detect abnormal movement patterns, such as falls or dizziness. It also real-time alerts caregivers or facility managers through phone calls, notifications, and automatic alarms.

By utilizing anonymized depth data rather than personal information, SAVVY prioritizes privacy while providing 24/7 monitoring. It offers real-time alerts whenever potential risks are detected, ensuring rapid response during emergencies like falls or distress in restroom settings.

UNIUNI’s engineering team developed SAVVY using non-identifiable Time-of-Flight (ToF) data and advanced deep learning algorithms to monitor behaviors and send instant alerts when intervention is required. The system’s performance metrics highlight its effectiveness, including a precision of 97.2%, a recall rate of 98.84%, and an F1 score of 98.01%. SAVVY provides real-time updates on restroom availability, cleanliness, and safety for seamless integration into restrooms, benefiting users and facility managers.

SAVVY is built for scalability, enabling its global deployment to enhance restroom safety and accessibility in public spaces. UNIUNI aims to use SAVVY to promote independence and dignity for individuals with physical disabilities while ensuring privacy and security in all public spaces.

At CES 2025, UNIUNI will present an interactive booth to demonstrate SAVVY’s capabilities. The company will focus on expanding its presence in smart city and accessibility markets and showcase how SAVVY aligns with the vision of creating accessible and secure public spaces.

After CES 2025, UNIUNI intends to leverage the insights and connections gained at the event to drive growth and innovation. With plans to enter key markets in Europe and the Middle East, the company aims to meet the growing demand for accessible infrastructure. Additionally, UNIUNI will integrate eco-friendly materials and energy-efficient technologies into its products to reduce environmental impact and ensure long-term sustainability.

UNIUNI plans to collaborate with governments, facilities, and businesses to scale its solutions and systematically change accessible infrastructure. By incorporating IoT and advanced machine learning, UNIUNI will improve real-time data analysis, enhance abnormality detection, and ensure safer conditions in public spaces.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
